info.name: Akatsuki's Draft API
info.description: Beginner-friendly collection covering every API. Run the folders in order, top to bottom (0 to 8). Tokens and IDs are saved automatically. Edit the "baseUrl" variable (collection > Variables tab) to switch between local and Vercel.

item.name: 0. Health check
item.description: Run these first. They prove the server (and database) is alive.

request.description: If this fails with 503, your MONGODB_URI or Atlas Network Access is wrong.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Register two normal users and log in. Logging in saves the JWT token for you automatically. The admin account is created with: npm run create-admin (see README).

request.description: Creates a normal user. If you run it twice you will get 409 "already registered" - that is fine.
A second user, used later to prove Bob cannot edit Alice's posts.
Needs the admin account from: npm run create-admin. If you get 401, the admin does not exist yet or the password differs.

item.name: 2. Posts (as Alice)
item.description: Create posts, list them, edit them. A post created with status "pending" is submitted for admin approval; "draft" just saves it privately.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "My first article",
  "description": "A short summary",
  "content": "this is my frist article. it have some grammer mistakes and is not very clear to read.",
  "image": "https://example.com/cover.jpg",
  "category": "Technology",
  "status": "pending"
}

{
  "title": "A post that will be rejected",
  "description": "For the reject test",
  "content": "This post exists so the admin can reject it.",
  "category": "General",
  "status": "pending"
}

{
  "title": "My private draft",
  "description": "Not submitted yet",
  "content": "Work in progress. Only I can see this.",
  "category": "General",
  "status": "draft"
}

request.description: Security test: users must not be able to publish their own posts.

exec: pm.test("only approved posts are listed", () => body.data.forEach(p => pm.expect(p.status).to.eql("approved")));

request.description: No token needed. Right now it will NOT contain your pending posts. Run it again after the admin approves.

exec: pm.test("includes my drafts and pending posts", () => pm.expect(body.count).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Expected 404 NOW because the post is still pending. After approval it returns 200 (see folder 4).

item.name: 3. Admin (as Admin)
item.description: Only the admin token works here. A normal user gets 403.

request.description: Only pending posts can be decided, so a second approval is refused.

item.name: 4. Public posts after approval
item.description: Now that the admin approved a post, the public can see it.

item.name: GET /posts (public) - now contains the approved post

exec: pm.test("approved post is listed", () => pm.expect(body.data.some(p => p._id === pm.collectionVariables.get("postId"))).to.eql(true));

item.name: 5. AI improvement (Gemini)
item.description: Needs GEMINI_API_KEY in your .env (or Vercel). Creates a NEW draft and never changes the original.

exec: pm.test("new draft with a NEW id", () => { pm.expect(body.data._id).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("postId")); pm.expect(body.data.status).to.eql("draft"); });

request.description: If you get 503, GEMINI_API_KEY is missing. If 502, check the key and GEMINI_MODEL. 429 means Gemini rate limit: wait a minute.

exec: pm.test("AI draft is in my drafts", () => pm.expect(body.data.some(p => p._id === pm.collectionVariables.get("aiPostId"))).to.eql(true));
pm.test("original text still has the typo", () => pm.expect(body.data.content).to.include("frist"));

request.description: Compare the content with what you originally wrote: it must be untouched.

item.name: 6. Update and delete my own posts

exec: pm.test("deleted post not listed", () => pm.expect(body.data.some(p => p._id === pm.collectionVariables.get("aiPostId"))).to.eql(false));

item.name: 7. Security checks (all of these SHOULD be refused)
item.description: Every request here is expected to fail. A green test means the protection works.

item.name: POST /auth/register with role "admin" -> still a normal user

exec: pm.test("never an admin", () => { if (pm.response.code === 201) { pm.expect(pm.response.json().user.role).to.eql("user"); } else { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(409); } });

request.description: The "role" field is ignored. Mallory becomes a normal "user" (or 409 if you ran this before).

item.name: 8. Cleanup (optional)
item.description: Deletes the test posts you created as Alice.

variable.description: Change to your Vercel URL (no trailing slash) to test the live site.
Must match ADMIN_EMAIL used with: npm run create-admin
Must match ADMIN_PASSWORD used with: npm run create-admin
